# True Aim: Full Documentation for LLMs

> Faster claims, smarter decisions, lower costs. Every claim assessed against the policy, every invoice benchmarked, every damage report prepared. Accurate, explainable outcomes in minutes.

## Company Overview

True Aim AG is a Swiss company based in Zug, Switzerland. True Aim is spun out of Yarowa, Switzerland's leading insurtech, and supported by Innosuisse, the innovation arm of the Swiss government, on the strength of the technology it has built.

Mission: to bring scalable trust to claims decisions. Every decision fast enough to matter, accurate enough to rely on and proven whenever it is questioned.

True Aim works for insurers, brokers, third-party administrators, warranty providers and claims technology providers.

### Awards

- Insurathon 2026: Norton Rose Fulbright crowned True Aim the most innovative InsurTech in the world for 2026.
- Innovationspreis der Schweizer Assekuranz: the Swiss insurance industry's innovation prize, awarded to the technology True Aim builds on.
- Digitaler Leuchtturm Versicherungen: Germany's digital lighthouse award for insurance, awarded to the technology True Aim builds on.
- Miglior InsurTech, IKN Awards: Best InsurTech at the IKN Insurance Awards, Italy, awarded to the technology True Aim builds on.

## Platform

**URL:** https://trueaim.ai/en/platform/

We turn the claim file into the finished piece of work: a settled claim, a benchmarked invoice or a completed damage report. AI reads the documents, the decision is calculated from your policy wording and every step is recorded. Your team keeps the final say.

### Automated Coverage Check

**URL:** https://trueaim.ai/en/platform/claims-decisioning/

True Aim checks the policy terms against the facts of the case and recommends whether the claim should be approved or denied. Where it is approved, the amount owed is calculated line by line, and the adjuster makes the final call. Each decision is recorded in the Decision Dossier: the inputs, the policy wording applied and the reasoning.

### Invoice Benchmarking

**URL:** https://trueaim.ai/en/platform/invoice-benchmarking/

Every invoice, quote and estimate is checked against the benchmark, by business line and by region. The claims team sees which lines are too high, by how much and why, with the reissue request already drafted. Lower-value invoices no longer go unchecked, and every saving is recorded line by line.

### Damage Reporting

**URL:** https://trueaim.ai/en/platform/damage-reporting/

Damage Reporting produces a damage estimate and the full scope of work at first notification, from the photographs and documents the customer sends. It prices the damage by region and lists every trade and task in the order the work must run. Assessors go on site only where a visit changes the answer.

### Otus, True Aim's claims specialist

**URL:** https://trueaim.ai/en/platform/otus/

Otus is an AI-powered expert for every team member, in every True Aim solution. Ask Otus anything about a claim, by voice or text, and the answer comes from the claim, the policy and the record. Otus drafts, explains and plans, and has no decision rights: the team decides.

---

## Technology

**URL:** https://trueaim.ai/en/technology/

### Neuro-Symbolic Architecture

True Aim's technology is not probabilistic and not a black box. Our hybrid approach combines:

- **Neural AI (Agentic Layer):** Handles document understanding, extraction, classification, and natural language processing tasks where flexibility is needed.
- **Symbolic AI (Deterministic Layer):** Executes policy logic, computes coverage, calculates costs, and produces decisions with mathematical certainty.

This combination ensures that while AI handles the messy, unstructured parts of claims processing, every actual decision is made by deterministic, auditable logic.

---

## Security and Compliance

**URL:** https://trueaim.ai/en/trust/

- ISO 27001: certified.
- SOC 2 Type II: audited (audit window 1 May to 31 July 2026, final report issued).
- GDPR, Swiss FADP and DORA: aligned.
- Every decision records the facts, the policy wording applied and the reasoning, so it can be reconstructed under audit, regulatory review or dispute.

---

## Results

From the vehicle warranty case study with NSA Services SA (https://trueaim.ai/en/case-studies/vehicle-warranty-claims/):

- 86% less expert time on a complex claim
- 83% less expert time on a simple claim
- 118% more claims handled by the same team
- 32 min saved on every claim

## Insights (Blog)

**Index:** https://trueaim.ai/en/blog/
**RSS:** https://trueaim.ai/feed.xml

- [The Problem with Automating Claims in Silos: Architectural Transparency and the Rise of the Agentic Claims Operation](https://trueaim.ai/en/blog/architectural-transparency-agentic-claims-operation/) (22 October 2026, Reuben John, CEO): A claim has never existed within the four walls of a single enterprise: policyholder, intermediary, carrier, repairer and adjuster each hold a fragment of the record. The case for one shared claim record under role-gated entitlements, where every decision carries line-level provenance and transparency between organisations ceases to be a courtesy and becomes an architectural guarantee.
- [Where the Language Model Does Not Belong: Designing Defensible AI in Claims Operations](https://trueaim.ai/en/blog/where-the-language-model-does-not-belong/) (6 October 2026, Reuben John, CEO): A claim decision is a chain of three kinds of steps: reading, computing and judging. Computing belongs to rules. A model earns its place in reading and, marked as probabilistic, in judging. The record keeps the boundary visible on every step.
- [The AI Claims Auditability Scorecard](https://trueaim.ai/en/blog/ai-claims-auditability-scorecard/) (10 September 2026, Reuben John, CEO): Twelve questions every claims leader should be able to answer about AI operating in their name, in four groups: provenance, reconstruction, human judgement and continuity, with the standard and how True Aim meets it under each.
- [AI Claims Handling Is Not High-Risk Under the EU AI Act. Here Is What Binds It Instead.](https://trueaim.ai/en/blog/ai-claims-handling-eu-ai-act-high-risk/) (28 July 2026): Claims handling is absent from Annex III. GDPR Article 22 binds it anyway.
- [Why Claims AI Pilots Stall Before Production Readiness](https://trueaim.ai/en/blog/why-claims-ai-pilots-stall/) (15 February 2026): Measurement discipline and production realism, not model accuracy, decide whether a pilot ships.
- [Auditability in Claims AI: Building Evidence Chains That Auditors Actually Accept](https://trueaim.ai/en/blog/auditability-evidence-chains/) (1 February 2025): The architecture behind provenance and reconstruction, and the requirements it satisfies.
- [Build vs Buy: What to Demand from IDP Vendors](https://trueaim.ai/en/blog/build-vs-buy-idp-vendors/) (1 February 2025): An evaluation framework for insurance teams choosing claims automation.
